Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the Run Chase! The Umpires and the players walk out to take the field as Pakistan Women come out to chase 141 runs in 20 overs. Muneeba Ali Siddiqi and Gull Feroza are the opening batters for Pakistan Women. It is Marufa Akter to start the new ball attack for Bangladesh Women. Let's Play!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

As the teams head into the break, Pakistan Women will be satisfied with their performance but it could have been better if they had maintained the same pressure till the end. For Bangladesh Women, the onus will be on their bowlers to pick early wickets and put the Pakistan Women under pressure. So, which side will come out on top? We shall find out soon. Chase coming up shortly...

The Bangladesh Women made a good start, however, the dismissal of Shathi Rani proved pivotal, leading to a marked slowdown in their scoring rate. The Pakistani bowlers capitalized on this momentum, claiming wickets at regular intervals and stifling any potential partnerships. However, a late surge from Shorna Akter, who provided some resistance with her quickfire 28, helped her team reach a more competitive total of 140 runs.

It was a good display of bowling from the Pakistan Women's team as they effectively contained the Bangladesh Women to a total of 140 runs. The Pakistani bowlers demonstrated a disciplined approach, employing a total of eight different bowlers throughout the match. Sadia Iqbal was the standout bowler for them as she picked two wickets. Key performances from Omaima Sohail, Tuba Hassan, Diana Bai and Nida Dar, who each claimed a wicket also played crucial roles in maintaining pressure on the batting side.

Short and wide outside the off stump from Sadia Iqbal. Shorna Akter slaps the ball to the left of covers and runs a couple to end the first innings for her team. Bangladesh Women manage to put up 140 runs in the first innings.

As the tournament approaches, Pakistani women are grouped with Sri Lanka, India, New Zealand, and Australia in Group A, while Bangladesh Women will compete in Group B alongside West Indies, England, South Africa, and Scotland. So, both teams will seek to enter the main event with a victory to bolster their momentum. Which side will come out on top? We shall find out soon. Toss and team news to follow shortly...

Meanwhile, Pakistan Women faced an upset against Scotland Women. After posting a modest total of 132 runs, with Omaima Sohail scoring 30, the bowlers struggled, leading to an 8-wicket defeat, with Nashra Sandhu being the sole wicket-taker.

In the opening warm-up for the Bangladesh Women, they bowled first against Sri Lanka Women, successfully restricting them to 143 runs, with Shoma Akter claiming 2 wickets for 19 runs. However, the batting lineup faltered, and despite a resilient 30-run innings from skipper Nigar Sultana, Bangladesh fell short, losing by 33 runs.

The ICC Women’s T20 World Cup is set to begin, with the warm-up games highlighting unexpected outcomes. In their final warm-up match, Bangladesh Women will take on Pakistan Women at the ICC Academy Ground No. 2 in Dubai.
... Match Day ...

The build-up to the ICC Women's T20 World Cup, 2024 continues with the warm-up matches. In the next match, Bangladesh Women take on Pakistan Women at the ICC Academy Ground No 2 in Dubai and it should be a fascinating encounter between the two sub-continental teams. These two teams have been in and around the knockout stages of the competition but haven't quite managed to go shoulder-to-shoulder with the big teams. In recent years, Bangladesh Women have challenged for the Asia Cup while Pakistan Women have fallen off a bit with the Lankans emerging as the Asian frontrunners alongside India and both these teams will be itching to replicate the success of their neighboring countries. Both teams come into this match on the back of a defeat in their previous round of warm-up matches as Bangladesh Women were undone by Asian champs Sri Lanka and Pakistan Women suffered a shock defeat at the hands of Scotland. Those results make this game even more crucial as both sides would want to go into the main event with a win behind their back. Let's see who comes out on top.
